learning_outcomes.text: Capacity for the writing and development of projects in the field of industrial engineering whose object is the construction, reform, repair, conservation, demolition, manufacturing, installation, assembly or exploitation of: structures, mechanical equipment, energy installations, electrical and electronic installations, industrial installations and plants and manufacturing and automation processes.
Capacity for the management of the activities object of the engineering projects described in the previous paragraph.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, which enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity and critical reasoning.
Ability to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering, both orally and in writing, and to all types of audiences.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans and other similar works.
Ability to handle specifications, regulations and mandatory standards.
Ability to analyze and assess the social and environmental impact of technical solutions.
Ability to apply quality principles and methods.
Ability to organize and plan in the field of business, and other institutions and organizations.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Ability to prevent occupational risks and protect the health and safety of workers and users.
Ability to know, select, criticize and use diverse sources of information.
Ability to work in a team.
Knowledge of the fundamentals and applications of digital electronics and microprocessors.
Applied knowledge of power electronics.
Ability to design analog, digital and power electronic systems.
Knowledge and ability for modeling and simulation of systems.
Knowledge of the fundamentals of electronics.
Analyze the operation and design combinational and sequential digital circuits using both fixed-function circuits and internally configurable digital circuits.
Assess the use of different resources and possibilities to carry out a digital design from a technical and economic point of view against certain initial specifications.

Distinguish and select the different architectures of microprocessor systems, with special emphasis on the particular case of microcontrollers and their most common internal functional blocks (ports, timers, A/D and D/A converters and CCP).
Analyze and design power electronic circuits.
Understand the basic principles of electronic power conversion, basic configurations, and switching, conversion, and control elements.

syllabus_topics: Microprocessor and microcontroller systems: architecture and internal blocks
Development tools and design procedure with microcontrollers
Software development of applications with microcontrollers
Interconnection and signal adaptation for input and output devices
Power topologies for energy conversion: AC/DC
Power topologies for energy conversion: DC/DC
Power topologies for energy conversion: DC/AC
Power topologies for energy conversion: AC/AC
P1- Simulation with LTspice of a controlled rectifier
P2- Simulation and assembly of a boost converter
P3- Simulation and assembly of an inverter
P4- Use of MPLAB and PROTEUS software
P5- Generation of timed visual effects on LEDs connected to the microcontroller port
P6- Use of the A/D conversion module
P7- Speed control of a DC motor using PWM modulation

assessment_methods.method: Active participation in the development of the course (P2)

assessment_rules: To pass the course in the ordinary call, a minimum of 5 out of 10 points must be obtained in the total final grade of the theoretical/practical exams. If all established minimums are reached, the final grade is calculated as N=(0.80 x T + 0.15 x P1 + 0.05 x P2). Otherwise, the grade will be the minimum between the calculated score and 4.0. For extraordinary calls, there will be a single theoretical/practical exam where a minimum of 5 out of 10 is required; a score below 5 will result in failure, and the final grade will be the minimum between the weighted score and 4.0. In extraordinary calls, grades for 'Exercises, assignments and reports' and 'Active participation' obtained during the current academic period are retained, up to a maximum of 2 points out of 10. For differentiated evaluation, the final grade is N=(0.80 x T + 0.20 x P) where P is the laboratory practical exam.
